steps.text: Bring quinoa and chicken broth to a boil in a saucepan; cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until liquid is completely absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat; stir pesto into quinoa. Fold tomato into mixture. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto Quinoa
raw_recipe.description: Quinoa is cooked in chicken broth, seasoned with pesto, and mixed with fresh tomato in this Ecuadorian side dish of quinoa with pesto.
raw_recipe.name: Pesto Quinoa

recipeInstructions.text: Bring quinoa and chicken broth to a boil in a saucepan; cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until liquid is completely absorbed, about 15 minutes.
Remove the saucepan from heat; stir pesto into quinoa. Fold tomato into mixture. Season with salt and pepper.

review.reviewBody: I hadn't thought of serving quinoa with pesto before so this recipe was a great idea starter for me. As well as the pesto, I added lots more tomatoes, sun dried tomatoes, chopped olives, chopped spinach, pine nuts and ate the whole thing with a little grated Parmesan on top. Delicious!
Giving it 4 stars for the idea but I modified it like so: 1C white rice + 2C chicken broth + chopped tomatoes + frozen spinach + lots of pesto + rice cooker = easiest meal ever.

Delicious. It makes a perfect recipe base. It would be fine as a side dish, but I wanted to make it into a meal, so I added cubed left over chicken breast, about 3/4 of a yellow pepper (any colour would be good), and about a cup of mushrooms. I also added an extra tbsp of pesto, and a bit of sea salt. It was so yummy. Next time I'm going to try it Greek style and take out the mushrooms and add olives and tomatoes. It even tastes good cold and would make a really nice salad. I will definitely be sharing this recipe.
Added chickpeas. Used canned diced tomatoes. Used chicken stock instead of water. Turned out really good.

I have made this for numerous parties and it us well liked. I do add more pesto than recipe calls for and use cherry tomatoes and mozzarella balls.. I always rinse my quinoa first and just cook in water not a fan of cooking it in stock.

This was great. I took some advice from the other reviewer and added about 1/2 cup sundried tomatoes, 1/4 cup pine nuts, and 5 oz chopped spinach. I topped it with grated Romano cheese and it was excellent!

I really liked this. I had some already cooked left over quinoa from another recipe (about 2 cups). I put in at least 2 heaping TBSP of basil, tomato pesto, a TBSP of sundried tomato bruscheta, chopped up about 1/4 cup pecans, 1/2 a tomato (all I had), 3/4 cup fresh spinach. It is really yummy. I will serve it on a bed of spinach as a side for dinner. Quinoa is so nutritious and whole grain.

This was so simple and tasty! I did add 3T of pesto, used veggie broth and a bunch of little grape tomatoes. Then I decided to add more - some baby spinach, black olives and garbanzo beans. Nice addition to my "quinoa recipes". Thanks.

Followed the directions for the most part. I ended up adding maybe 3.5 tbsp of Pesto though. I also added chickpeas and shredded Parmesan. I couldn't stop eating while I was cooking. Oh almost forgot I added some lemon juice too. Eating as I'm trying this out. Thinking I might add feta cheese into one of my lunch bowls.

I thought this was a bit dry, but my fiance loved it and wouldn't stop raving about it, so am giving it five stars. I did make several changes. Instead of cherry tomatoes, I used sun-dried tomatoes. Also threw in some kalamata olives. Topped it with chopped walnuts, but would use pine nuts next time (we didn't have any). I put in extra pesto to make it less dry, and then even added some flax oil. Topped it with feta.

This was very yummy and a great way to introduce my family to Quinoa. I added pine nuts, sliced little grape tomatos, garlic, and right before serving tossed in some arugula. I think my soup stock was a tad too salty so next time I'll use reduced sodium chicken broth. My daughter wanted it the next day for her lunch box!
This is delicious just as written! I did cut the recipe in half with no problem. Thanks for such a great, easy recipe!
I added some citrus pucker seasoning and used tri-colored quinoa. It was colorful and delicious
Didn't have pine nuts so left them out. Still great!
Used 4 tablespoons of pesto & added olives.
I really like this recipe, not only very tasty, it was fast and easier than making a pasta dish. It will a go to in this household.

This was very easy and very good. Couple of changes that I made – – was out of chicken stock so I used vegetable stock. Turned out very good; I added a little bit more pesto than what was called for as well as a little bit of olive oil. Delicious.

I like that this is an easy quick recipe, great for when you are too buys to make something more. complicated. I doubled the pesto as some others had recommended. Next time, I will try adding olives and Parmesan to it.
Great new side to add to our meals, but with black beans, it became a main course. I took it to a party and it was a huge hit with requests for the recipe!
Did not make any changes and will make it again
